articles.title: Trump sugere 'sacrificar Los Angeles ou San Diego' em guerra contra o Irã; Oposição critica: 'Perturbado, boca maldita' | G1
articles.standfirst: Fala em comício no Nebraska gerou nova polêmica para o presidente dos EUA. Governador da Califórnia e prefeita de Los Angeles criticaram Trump.
articles.summary: Fala em comício no Nebraska gerou nova polêmica para o presidente dos EUA. Governador da Califórnia e prefeita de Los Angeles criticaram Trump.
articles.body:
Presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, discursa em comício no Nebraska em 5 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Nathan Howard

O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , envolveu-se em mais uma polêmica ao sugerir as cidades de Los Angeles e San Diego como possíveis alvos de ataques do Irã. Diversas autoridades da oposição democrata, incluindo o governo local, criticaram Trump.

“Este é um pequeno preço a pagar pela segurança do mundo, pela segurança do nosso país", afirmou Trump sobre a guerra contra o Irã. "Eles poderiam destruir uma cidade [dos EUA]. Deixem que destruam Los Angeles. Deixem que destruam San Diego. É um preço muito pequeno a pagar e, muito em breve, tudo isso [a guerra] terá acabado. Basicamente, já está quase acabando”, completou.

A fala ocorreu em um comício no Nebraska na noite de segunda-feira, onde Trump tenta garantir o sucesso eleitoral dos candidatos republicanos no estado nos midterms, as eleições de meio de mandato, que ocorrerão no início de novembro.

Los Angeles e San Diego ficam na Califórnia, no oeste dos EUA, e são governadas por democratas. Juntas, elas têm cerca de 5,2 milhões de habitantes.

Diversas autoridades norte-americanas criticaram Trump pelas declarações. O governador da Califórnia, o democrata Gavin Newsom, afirmou que o presidente norte-americano é "perturbado e perigoso".

"Depois de enviar a Guarda Nacional e os fuzileiros navais para ocupar a Califórnia, Donald Trump agora está dizendo que nossos inimigos estrangeiros deveriam 'acabar com' Los Angeles e San Diego. Ele é perturbado e perigoso", afirmou.

A prefeita de Los Angeles, Karen Bass, também reagiu: “Deixe Los Angeles fora da sua boca maldita” , escreveu nas redes sociais nesta terça (6).

Gavin Newsom e Donald Trump — Foto: Reuters

O senador democrata Alex Padilla, que representa a Califórnia, acusou Trump de "chamar um ataque em território americano e colocar milhões de cidadãos em risco". Ele lembrou também que um soldado de Nebraska morreu na guerra contra o Irã.

"Pelo menos 19 militares morreram na guerra não autorizada de Trump contra o Irã. Agora Trump está convidando um ataque em território americano, colocando milhões de americanos e centenas de milhares de militares americanos em risco, enquanto tenta fazer com que os americanos comemorem um ataque contra o próprio país. Que tipo de comandante [de um país] faz isso?", afirmou Padilla.

Horas depois, na terça-feira, a Casa Branca rejeitou as críticas e defendeu a fala de Trump. "Ele estava dizendo que os EUA estão lutando para IMPEDIR que o Irã tenha a capacidade de destruir Los Angeles e San Diego com uma arma nuclear — o que eles fariam se tivessem a oportunidade".

Na contramão da fala da Casa Branca, não há qualquer indício de que o Irã teria mísseis capazes de chegar às cidades dos EUA , nem mesmo antes da guerra, segundo especialistas em questões militares.

O prefeito de San Diego, Todd Gloria, não havia se manifestado publicamente sobre a fala de Trump até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Como a guerra aumentou a violência sexual e os casamentos forçados de meninas e mulheres em Gaza | G1
articles.standfirst: Convivência com desconhecidos e falta de privacidade nos abrigos têm sido acompanhadas por relatos de assédio e abuso sexual. Muitas famílias veem o casamento das filhas como uma forma de protegê-las e preservar sua reputação.
articles.summary: Convivência com desconhecidos e falta de privacidade nos abrigos têm sido acompanhadas por relatos de assédio e abuso sexual. Muitas famílias veem o casamento das filhas como uma forma de protegê-las e preservar sua reputação.
articles.body:
Relatórios recentes do UNFPA apontam forte aumento da violência contra mulheres e meninas na Faixa de Gaza — Foto: REUTERS

Relatórios recentes do Fundo de População das Nações Unidas (UNFPA, na sigla em inglês) apontam um forte aumento da violência contra mulheres e meninas na Faixa de Gaza, incluindo casos de casamento precoce e forçado.

Um dos documentos, elaborado com dados reunidos por dez organizações, afirma que a crise prolongada em Gaza, devastada pela guerra, "criou condições que expõem mulheres e meninas a riscos cada vez maiores de violência de gênero".

O relatório também alerta para uma "forte escalada" dos casos de casamento precoce e forçado no segundo trimestre deste ano. A Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU) considera as duas práticas como formas de violência de gênero.

Outro relatório reúne depoimentos de 230 mulheres que vivem em campos superlotados para deslocados na Cidade de Gaza e em Khan Younis e descreve os episódios de violência que elas sofreram ou testemunharam.

Atenção: esta reportagem contém detalhes que podem ser perturbadores para alguns leitores.

Uma mulher que vive em uma escola transformada em abrigo em Gaza relata que vítimas de estupro muitas vezes são obrigadas a se casar com os próprios agressores para evitar a vergonha e o escândalo. "Quando um caso de estupro é descoberto em uma escola, no dia seguinte há casamento e comemoração no local", diz ela.

Outra mulher conta que, no ano passado, durante o período de fome, "um homem deu a filha de 14 anos em casamento em troca de dois sacos de farinha, para que ele e os [outros] filhos pudessem comer". Seis mulheres que vivem em diferentes campos de deslocados relataram situações semelhantes, algo que seria impensável antes do início do conflito entre Israel e o Hamas, em 2023.

Ainda é difícil chegar a números precisos, mas o UNFPA afirma que os casos registrados de casamento precoce e forçado aumentaram 123% no segundo trimestre deste ano em relação aos três primeiros meses. Nos casos de casamento precoce ou infantil, as meninas tinham entre 12 e 17 anos.

"As tendências são chocantes", afirma Nestor Owomuhangi, representante do UNFPA para a Palestina. Segundo ele, as condições extremas enfrentadas por Gaza nos últimos três anos — com dezenas de milhares de mortos, destruição em larga escala e sucessivos deslocamentos da população — romperam estruturas sociais básicas. "Tudo se deteriorou... não há sistema."

Embora os mercados de alimentos tenham reaberto, muitas pessoas não têm dinheiro para comprar os produtos disponíveis. A pobreza extrema e a fome continuam, e grande parte da população depende de doações. Quase todos os mais de 2 milhões de habitantes de Gaza foram expulsos de suas casas, e a maioria vive hoje em acampamentos de tendas em condições precárias ou em prédios danificados. Os serviços públicos entraram em colapso em grande parte, e os ataques aéreos israelenses continuaram apesar do cessar-fogo.

Cerca de 1,2 milhão de palestinos em Gaza vivem em tendas ou abrigos improvisados — Foto: Reuters

Antes da guerra, as meninas eram maioria e tinham desempenho melhor que o dos meninos em todos os níveis de ensino depois da escola primária em Gaza. Agora, com as escolas fechadas por longos períodos, muitas crianças deixaram de estudar. Os meninos sofrem pressão para conseguir trabalhos informais e ajudar no sustento da família; para as meninas, a falta de segurança se tornou uma preocupação ainda maior.

Em uma sociedade conservadora, a convivência com desconhecidos e a falta de privacidade nos abrigos têm sido acompanhadas por mais relatos de assédio e abuso sexual. Muitas famílias veem o casamento das filhas como uma forma de protegê-las e preservar sua reputação. O relatório do UNFPA, baseado em pesquisas realizadas no fim de 2025 e no início de 2026, mostra que meninas que ficaram órfãs durante a guerra estão especialmente vulneráveis.

Uma mulher entrevistada para o relatório em um campo de deslocados na Cidade de Gaza conta que foi ao casamento de duas meninas de sua família, de apenas 14 e 15 anos.

"Os tios as casaram muito novas. Sabe por quê? Porque o pai e a mãe delas foram martirizados, e os tios queriam se livrar da responsabilidade e das despesas", disse a mulher. "Por Deus, elas não entendem o que é casamento nem o que é a vida."

O Women's Affairs Center in Gaza, uma ONG palestina que trabalha em parceria com o UNFPA, e outros grupos de apoio registraram casos graves de meninas que foram casadas, sofreram abusos e, muitas vezes, engravidaram. Segundo essas organizações, adolescentes muito jovens correm risco bem maior de sofrer abortos espontâneos e de dar à luz bebês com baixo peso do que mulheres adultas.

"Estamos vendo um aumento enorme das gestações na adolescência por causa do casamento infantil", diz Owomuhangi, do UNFPA para a Palestina. "Estamos falando de uma criança cujo corpo ainda não está completamente desenvolvido para levar uma gestação adiante, que passa fome, vive em condições insalubres, não sabe cuidar de um bebê e nem sequer sabe cuidar de si mesma. As consequências dessa gravidez são sempre muito, muito graves."

A ONU e a maioria das organizações humanitárias consideram casamento precoce aquele que envolve meninas com menos de 18 anos. Antes mesmo da guerra, esse tipo de união já era mais comum entre palestinos na Faixa de Gaza, governada pelo Hamas, do que na Cisjordânia ocupada, embora estivesse em queda.

Em Gaza, a idade mínima para o casamento é 17 anos, mas a lei permite exceções com o consentimento dos pais e autorização de um juiz. Os tribunais podem aprovar casamentos a partir dos 14 anos e sete meses. Mas um especialista local em direito islâmico (sharia) disse à BBC que essas "salvaguardas legais" deixaram de funcionar quando os tribunais islâmicos — responsáveis por questões familiares entre muçulmanos — ficaram fechados durante boa parte da guerra.

Cerca de 700 mil crianças ficaram quase três anos sem frequentar aulas presenciais regulares — Foto: Anadolu via Getty Images

A BBC conversou com famílias em que jovens acabaram se casando depois de perder parentes na guerra. Zuhair, de 25 anos, conta que os tios o pressionaram a se casar com uma jovem de 16 anos de sua família depois que o pai dela — seu único responsável — morreu em um ataque aéreo israelense.

Ao ser questionado sobre por que aceitou o casamento, respondeu: "Um dos motivos foi que não havia ninguém para cuidar dela. Esse foi o primeiro ponto".

"Se não fosse a guerra, ela ainda estaria sob os cuidados do pai, levando uma vida de adolescente e frequentando a escola", acrescenta Zuhair. "Ela ainda pensa como uma criança. Sente falta da escola, da família, dos amigos. Sente falta até de ficar em casa."

Outro casal conta que permitiu que o filho de 17 anos se casasse com a prima, de 16, depois que o filho mais velho e o pai da menina morreram. A adolescente está grávida e não voltará à escola. "Ela precisa cuidar do filho", diz o sogro. "Continuar estudando não teria mais utilidade para ela."

Organizações humanitárias afirmam que melhorar as condições de assistência em Gaza reduziria significativamente os riscos enfrentados pelas mulheres — Foto: EPA

A violência sexual em Gaza continua sendo fortemente subnotificada, principalmente por medo de estigma e represálias. Avaliações de segurança da ONU mostram que mulheres e meninas ficam particularmente expostas à noite, o que leva muitas delas a evitar os banheiros dos campos.

O relatório mais recente do grupo de trabalho coordenado UNFPA afirma que os casos de violência sexual, incluindo estupro e agressão sexual, "atingiram um nível crítico em Gaza". Entre abril e junho de 2026, esse tipo de violência respondeu por 2,7% de todos os casos de violência de gênero registrados, ante 2,1% no trimestre anterior. Em números absolutos, o total de casos aumentou 61%.

O aumento também pode estar relacionado às campanhas de conscientização e à ampliação dos canais para denúncias confidenciais. Os dados mostram que a maioria das vítimas era formada por mulheres de 18 a 59 anos. Meninas adolescentes correspondiam a 8% dos casos, e homens adultos, a 5%.

Viúvas e mulheres cujos maridos estão presos ou desaparecidos também estão mais expostas a abuso e exploração sexual. Hoje, quase um em cada quatro domicílios é sustentado por uma mulher, proporção que dobrou em relação ao período anterior à guerra.

"Uma viúva procurava uma tenda quando um representante [do campo] disse: 'Eu te dou uma tenda, coloco você no nosso campo e você pode passar a noite comigo'", relata uma mulher da Cidade de Gaza entrevistada para o relatório do UNFPA.

Organizações humanitárias afirmam que melhorar as condições de assistência em Gaza reduziria de forma significativa os riscos enfrentados pelas mulheres. Elas pedem que Israel autorize a entrada de abrigos de melhor qualidade e de equipamentos para melhorar as latrinas, o saneamento e a iluminação. Israel restringe a entrada de itens que considera passíveis de uso tanto civil quanto militar.

Também há iniciativas para ampliar o acesso à educação e à saúde, além de planos de longo prazo para campanhas de combate à violência doméstica e ao casamento infantil. A vida de muitas pessoas em Gaza já mudou de forma irreversível, mas as mulheres dizem esperar por um futuro em que possam se sentir, ao menos, mais seguras.

articles.title: Lituânia dá 1º passo para permitir armas nucleares; Rússia repudia | G1
articles.standfirst: Parlamento lituano aprovou de forma preliminar acabar com lei que proíbe armazenar armas nucleares em seu território. Votação derradeira está marcada para janeiro. Lituânia integra a Otan e faz fronteira com a Rússia.
articles.summary: Parlamento lituano aprovou de forma preliminar acabar com lei que proíbe armazenar armas nucleares em seu território. Votação derradeira está marcada para janeiro. Lituânia integra a Otan e faz fronteira com a Rússia.
articles.body:
Presidente da Rússia, Vladimir Putin (à esquerda), e primeiro-ministro da Lituânia, Mindaugas Sinkevicius. — Foto: Ramil Sitdikov/Annegret Hilse/Reuters

O Parlamento da Lituânia aprovou nesta terça-feira (6), em votação preliminar, suspender uma lei que proíbe armazenar armas nucleares em seu território. A Rússia considerou o movimento lituano como uma provocação e prometeu retaliar caso a medida seja aprovada em definitivo.

A medida foi aprovada pelo Parlamento lituano, com 106 votos favoráveis de 141 possíveis, mas para derrubar a lei e mudar a Constituição do país será necessária uma nova aprovação em uma segunda votação, que está marcada para 12 de janeiro.

A Lituânia, que integra a Otan e faz fronteira com a Rússia, está entre os países mais ameaçados por uma eventual expansão da guerra da Ucrânia. O sentimento também é compartilhado pelos outros países bálticos, que temem uma invasão russa.

O presidente lituano, Gitanas Nauseda, disse em julho que os partidos políticos haviam chegado a um acordo sobre um plano para suspender a proibição, em um sinal de como a Rússia está redefinindo os cálculos de segurança na região.

Ainda em julho, Nauseda disse que não havia planos imediatos para armazenar armas nucleares no país, mas que a retirada da norma permitiria que o país tomasse medidas caso a situação de segurança mudasse. Ele afirmou também que a Lituânia continuará sendo signatária do Tratado de Não Proliferação de Armas Nucleares.

Em resposta à medida, o Kremlin afirmou nesta terça que o movimento do governo lituano poderia levar a uma nova etapa de escalada de tensões na região e indicou um eventual posicionamento de armas nucleares dos Estados Unidos no país báltico. Por conta disso, o governo Putin afirmou que se veria forçado a tomar ações para preservar sua segurança nacional.

“Se a infraestrutura militar daquele que, na prática, é o principal país da Otan (os EUA) estiver se aproximando de nossas fronteiras, então, é claro, isso não pode ser visto como outra coisa senão um passo em direção à escalada das tensões”, afirmou o porta-voz do Kremlin, Dmitry Peskov.

“O mesmo se aplica à instalação de armas nucleares no território de um Estado vizinho. Nenhum desses acontecimentos contribuirá para a estabilidade e a previsibilidade no continente europeu; pelo contrário, eles, para nosso grande pesar, representarão mais uma escalada significativa das tensões”, acrescentou Peskov.

Os EUA mantêm na Lituânia um batalhão blindado de quase 1.000 militares desde 2019, em rotações alternadas, o que significa que as tropas chegam e deixam o país a cada poucos meses.

articles.title: Polícia do Vietnã prende quadrilha que roubava gatos para vender carne | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo os investigadores, os animais - cerca de 4 a 10 por noite - eram levados de bairros residenciais pela madrugada; 12 homens foram presos.
articles.summary: Segundo os investigadores, os animais - cerca de 4 a 10 por noite - eram levados de bairros residenciais pela madrugada; 12 homens foram presos.
articles.body:
Um dos gatos resgatados está sendo cuidado em abrigo de um grupo de direitos dos animais — Foto: Wagwel/Humane World for Animals via AP

A polícia da cidade de Ho Chi Minh, no Vietnã , prendeu 12 homens suspeitos de comandar uma quadrilha que roubava gatos para vendê-los para consumo de carne, informou a mídia estatal vietnamita nesta terça-feira (6).

Segundo os investigadores, os acusados confessaram que cerca de 2.700 animais foram vítimas do esquema.

O líder da quadrilha, Luu Thanh Binh, de 39 anos, trabalhava com fornecedores que recrutavam outras pessoas para percorrer bairros residenciais de motocicleta entre as 23h e as 4h da manhã, à procura dos gatos e capturando de quatro a dez por noite.

Em julho, outra operação policial já havia encontrado 50 felinos e dezenas de armadilhas; 13 deles voltaram aos seus donos. O restante está sendo cuidado por uma organização sem fins lucrativos de defesa dos animais enquanto as autoridades tentavam identificar seus proprietários.

O consumo de carne de cachorro e gato é praticado em algumas partes da Ásia, mas diminuiu muito ao longo dos anos.

No Vietnã, ele é permitido, mas os restaurantes que oferecem precisam de licenças que comprovem a origem dos animais. Em 2024, mais de 250 mil pessoas assinaram uma petição pedindo o fim do comércio.

Segundo a organização de proteção animal Humane World for Animals, estima-se que 5 milhões de cães e 1 milhão de gatos sejam capturados, roubados, traficados e abatidos para consumo de carne no Vietnã todos os anos.

articles.title: Alesp teve 55 dos 94 deputados reeleitos; renovação será de 41,5% | G1
articles.standfirst: PL amplia bancada e segue como principal força da Casa. Entre os novatos estão a campeã de votos Eduarda Campopiano e ex-prefeitos de cidades paulistas.
articles.summary: PL amplia bancada e segue como principal força da Casa. Entre os novatos estão a campeã de votos Eduarda Campopiano e ex-prefeitos de cidades paulistas.
articles.body:
A Assembleia Legislativa de São Paulo (Alesp) passará por uma renovação de 41,5% a partir de fevereiro de 2027. Dos 94 deputados estaduais eleitos nas eleições deste domingo (4), 39 não integram a atual legislatura. Ao todo, 14 legendas terão representação na Casa no próximo mandato (veja lista completa abaixo) .

Apesar da renovação, a principal característica da próxima legislatura será a manutenção da correlação de forças que marcou os últimos quatro anos. Dos 77 deputados que tentaram permanecer na Assembleia, 55 conseguiram se reeleger. A maior parte deles integra partidos que apoiam o governador reeleito Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) , que seguirá contando com ampla maioria na Assembleia.

A principal bancada continuará sendo a do PL. O partido passará de 21 para 27 deputados estaduais e seguirá como a maior força política da Casa . Na oposição, o destaque ficou com o crescimento do PSOL, que saltou de cinco para nove parlamentares. Já o PT perdeu uma cadeira, mas manteve a segunda maior bancada da Alesp, com 16 deputados.

Plenário da Alesp durante discussão de projetos — Foto: Rodrigo Romeo/ Alesp

O cientista político Hilton Fernandes avalia que a composição eleita fortalece a capacidade de articulação do governador, mas pode reduzir o peso da fiscalização exercida pela oposição. Segundo ele, uma base excessivamente ampla pode enfraquecer o papel de controle exercido pelo Legislativo.

"O governador precisa prestar contas para a Assembleia. Se não tem uma base suficientemente forte de oposição que vá buscar os dados para fazer uma fiscalização mais bem feita, nós também corremos o risco de o governador estar com força demais. E isso também não é bom, tanto pro estado como pra democracia em gera", afirmou.

Dos 39 parlamentares eleitos para ocupar as cadeiras de outros deputados, quatro já passaram pela Assembleia e retornarão em 2027: Douglas Garcia (União Brasil), João Paulo Rillo (PT), Luiza Erundina (PSOL) e Reinaldo Alguz (MDB).

Outros 35 assumirão o cargo de deputado estadual pela primeira vez. O partido que mais contribuirá para essa renovação será o PL, com 11 estreantes, entre eles Eduarda Campopiano, que recebeu 1,95 milhão de votos e foi a candidata mais votada para a Alesp .

O PT terá quatro estreantes na bancada estadual: Duda Hidalgo, Leonardo Grandini e Rodrigo Mar.

A próxima legislatura também contará com vereadores da capital paulista que chegarão pela primeira vez à Alesp: Thammy Miranda (PSD), Marina Bragante (PSB) e Keit Lima (PSOL).

Também estreiam na Casa nomes como a ativista trans Sofia Favero (PSOL), terceira candidata mais votada do estado; Rogério Lins (Podemos), ex-prefeito de Osasco; Renata Sene (Republicanos), ex-prefeita de Francisco Morato; e Rodrigo Ashiuchi (PL), ex-prefeito de Suzano.

Os dois candidatos mais votados dessa eleição foram "puxadores de votos" relevantes para suas legendas.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Traffic snarls hit several parts of Delhi-NCR on Tuesday as restrictions for the INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission added to congestion in central Delhi, while commuters on other key stretches reported heavy traffic and prolonged delays.The INDIA bloc MPs marched from the Parliament House complex towards the Election Commission headquarters to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Delhi Traffic Police had put special arrangements in place from 8am, regulating or diverting traffic around Connaught Place, Patel Chowk, Parliament Street, Jantar Mantar Road, Ashoka Road and adjoining stretches.Commuters were advised to avoid unnecessary travel through the affected areas and expect barricading, diversions and congestion.Heavy traffic was also reported on the Ring Road near AIIMS-Safdarjung Hospital, in and around Connaught Place, on Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Marg in Old Delhi and on the Delhi-Noida corridor near Crowne Plaza, Mayur Vihar.Connaught Place, Old Delhi see heavy congestionThe traffic police separately responded to complaints of prolonged congestion in and around Connaught Place, saying personnel had been deployed at critical junctions and were carrying out active traffic regulation and decongestion measures.On Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Marg in Old Delhi, the traffic police said movement was slow because of prevailing traffic arrangements and high traffic volume. Personnel were deployed at key points to regulate traffic and ease the congestion.On Ring Road near AIIMS-Safdarjung Hospital, the traffic police said it had alerted the concerned traffic circle for immediate deployment and active regulation at critical junctions, merging points and bottlenecks.It also said special attention was being given to ensuring the unhindered movement of ambulances and emergency vehicles.Delhi-Noida corridor also hitCommuters on the Delhi-Noida corridor near Crowne Plaza in Mayur Vihar also reported heavy congestion.Responding to a commuter's complaint on X, the Delhi Traffic Police said personnel were actively regulating movement and had been deployed at critical merging points and bottlenecks to ensure smoother traffic flow.The traffic police also responded to complaints about congestion around Krishna Menon Marg, Kartavya Path and adjoining roads, saying restrictions were being imposed only when required for operational or security reasons and for the minimum possible duration.VIP movements add to Delhi's recurring traffic problemThe traffic disruption comes a day after the movement of Swiss President Guy Parmelin to Rajghat led to road restrictions and lengthy delays for commuters in central Delhi.During Parmelin's Rajghat visit on Monday, commuters reported being stuck for extended periods around ITO and other key stretches.A recent VIP movement involving Russian President Vladimir Putin had, however, shown that traffic could keep moving despite security restrictions, with congestion clearing relatively quickly.The issue has raised questions over whether better advance planning, deployment and communication can reduce the impact of such movements on daily commuters.Why is traffic restricted today?The immediate trigger in central Delhi was the INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission over the SIR exercise. articles.title: Airbnb was born in Texas in 2006 when two hosts inflated three airbeds, 20 years later Airbnb is spending millions to build 200-plus housing units in Austin
articles.summary: Airbnb started with three airbeds and a simple idea to help pay the rent.
articles.body: Airbnb started with three airbeds and a simple idea to help pay the rent. Nearly 20 years later, the company is putting millions of dollars into housing in Austin, Texas. Last month, Airbnb announced a $6.4 million investment in a project that will support the construction of 201 affordable housing units in the city. The investment is part of the company's new Housing Accelerator programme, which Airbnb says will combine funding, policy changes and new ideas to help build more homes. The Austin project is the first local housing investment under the programme.How Airbnb went from three airbeds to a housing projectAirbnb says its story began when two hosts inflated three airbeds and created a website to help pay their rent. The company has since grown into a global short-term rental platform, with millions of hosts earning income through their homes.But Airbnb now says many people in the same communities where its hosts live are struggling to find homes they can afford. That has prompted the company to take a new approach to the housing problem.Airbnb announced the Housing Accelerator on September 14, saying it is committing an initial $250 million in last-dollar financing. The company expects that money to help unlock more than $5 billion in capital over the next 10 years for housing projects. The programme will also support changes to zoning, permits and building rules that can make it easier to construct homes.Airbnb will invest $6.4 million in 201 affordable homesThe first investment will go to the St. John redevelopment project at 800 E. St. John Avenue in Austin. Airbnb said its $6.4 million investment will support 201 affordable housing units. The project is part of a larger development that will include a second building with 325 mixed-income homes. Together, the two projects are expected to provide more than 500 housing units, along with retail space, a park and public art.The affordable housing project is also important because of how long the site has remained unused. The City of Austin has owned the property since 2013, but the site had remained empty for nearly 20 years.Construction had already received community support and tax incentives through a Texas affordable housing programme. However, the project was held up for five years because it could not secure enough funding. Airbnb's investment is intended to fill that funding gap and allow construction to begin.Airbnb also wants Austin to change its housing rulesAirbnb said money alone will not solve the housing shortage. The company is also backing local housing policy changes through organisations such as AURA, an Austin-based pro-housing group.AURA has campaigned for rules that would allow up to three homes per lot and smaller minimum lot sizes. Such changes could make it easier to build smaller and more affordable starter homes. The group also wants Austin to allow more "missing middle" housing, a term generally used for homes such as duplexes, townhouses and other smaller multi-home developments that sit between single-family houses and large apartment buildings.Airbnb's funding will allow AURA to hire its first paid staff member after operating as an all-volunteer organisation for more than a decade.Kirk Watson, Mayor of Austin, said, "Austin leads the national conversation and the actual outcomes on housing because we're doing what it takes to build. I'm glad to see Airbnb investing in housing projects like St. John's. Expanding housing takes all of us. When a company like Airbnb steps up and works alongside local organizations, community leaders, and the city, you get real outcomes."José “Chito” Vela, Mayor Pro Tem and Councilmember for District 4, said, “Austin's housing shortage demands a collaborative approach. The St. John’s project shows what’s possible when the public sector, private sector, and community partners come together to build more housing and ensure affordability. I’m proud that Austin is the first city where Airbnb is making this kind of local investment.”AURA President Zach Faddis said, “AURA is grateful to Airbnb for their partnership and commitment to strengthening communities here in Austin. For more than a decade, we have advanced reforms to address the root cause of Austin’s housing crisis: the simple fact that we have made it too difficult to build enough homes for everyone. Airbnb has been a real partner in working with communities to address that issue head on, and we welcome their generous support for the work we do to advance pro-housing policies.”You use AI every day. articles.body: NOIDA: A video showing a woman being escorted out of a store at DLF Mall of India in Sector 18 after she was allegedly accused of stealing ghee and refined cooking oil has gone viral on social media. Police and the mall management, however, have not confirmed that the woman stole any items and said she had paid for the products.The video, which is around 30 seconds long, shows two female security guards stopping a woman inside the store and taking her away. The woman can be seen covering her face as she walks out of the premises. During the incident, a store employee can be heard accusing her of stealing goods.Several claims accompanying the video on social media allege that the woman had been visiting the store for around a month and had allegedly taken ghee and refined oil on multiple occasions without paying. Some posts also claim that her activities had been captured on the store’s CCTV cameras.However, no CCTV footage supporting these allegations has been shared along with the viral video. The video itself also does not show the woman stealing any item or leaving the store without making a payment.Following the circulation of the video, information was sought from Sector 20 police. Police said their preliminary inquiry found that the woman had paid for the items she had taken from the store. The mall management also conveyed the same information to the police, officials said.“The woman had paid for the items. The allegations being made on social media have not been established,” police said.The video has triggered a range of reactions on social media, with several users sharing and commenting on the incident. It has reportedly been shared by more than 100 people.Police said the footage currently establishes only that the woman was stopped by security personnel and that a store employee accused her of theft. The circumstances in which the woman was stopped and what transpired inside the store cannot be conclusively determined from the viral video alone.Officials said claims made on social media should not be treated as established facts unless supported by evidence. Police also said that neither the mall nor the store management has submitted a formal complaint regarding theft in connection with the incident so far.Police are examining the available information and other aspects of the incident. articles.title: A Michigan homeowner owed $3,000 in taxes, but the county sold her home and kept all $23,500; an appeals court has now reopened her legal fight to recover the surplus from the foreclosure
articles.summary: A $3,000 tax debt ended with a Michigan homeowner losing her home and the county keeping $23,500 from its sale.
articles.body: A $3,000 tax debt ended with a Michigan homeowner losing her home and the county keeping $23,500 from its sale. Years later, her fight to recover that money is back in court. The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, in an October 5, 2026 opinion in Cunningham v. Allegan County, overturned a lower-court dismissal and sent the case back for further proceedings. The court said the lower court used the wrong legal approach when deciding whether Denise Thompson’s federal claim was filed too late. The ruling does not mean Thompson has won the $23,500; instead, it gives her lawsuit another chance to move forward.How the foreclosure dispute beganThompson’s case stems from Michigan’s former tax-foreclosure system. Counties could foreclose on properties when owners failed to pay their property taxes, sell those properties and, under the system in place at the time, keep the money left over after the tax debt was satisfied. That is what happened to Thompson, according to the Sixth Circuit. She owed about $3,000 in taxes, but Allegan County foreclosed on her home and later sold it. The county kept the entire $23,500 in sale proceeds, an amount substantially higher than the debt that triggered the foreclosure.Thompson was not the only homeowner affected. Gary and Josette Day also lost property through Allegan County foreclosures in 2013 and 2014. Their claims eventually became part of a broader legal battle over whether Michigan counties could retain surplus money generated by tax-foreclosure sales.The class-action case that changed the timelineIn December 2014, Michigan taxpayers filed a class action known as Wayside Church v. County of Van Buren. The plaintiffs argued that counties violated the Constitution’s Takings Clause by keeping surplus proceeds after selling foreclosed properties. Thompson and the Days were unnamed members of the plaintiff class, while Allegan County was initially an unnamed member of the defendant class. The lawsuit was dismissed in 2015 but reopened in 2019 after developments in the law.In July 2023, Thompson and the Days opted out of a class settlement because they wanted to pursue individual claims against Allegan County. They filed those lawsuits in March 2024. That timing became the central issue in the case.Why the county said the lawsuit was too lateAllegan County argued that Thompson and the Days had missed the deadline for bringing their federal claims. The district court agreed and dismissed the claims as time-barred. The homeowners, however, argued that their participation in the Wayside class action had paused the statute of limitations. They had remained part of that litigation for more than eight years and argued that the clock should not have been running against them throughout that entire period. The Sixth Circuit agreed that the lower court had taken the wrong approach.What the appeals court decidedJudge Amul Thapar, writing for the Sixth Circuit, said Michigan law controls the tolling issue because the homeowners brought their claims under federal civil-rights law, but such claims generally borrow the applicable state statute of limitations. The court found that Michigan’s tolling rules could apply to the Wayside litigation. It also concluded that the 2019 reopening of the class action meant the tolling period could continue rather than simply ending when the case was dismissed in 2015.That matters because, if the Wayside case paused the clock until Thompson and the Days opted out, their individual lawsuits could have been filed within the applicable deadline. But the appeals court did not decide that the claims are definitely timely.The question still left for the lower courtThe Sixth Circuit said another issue needs to be examined: whether Allegan County had sufficient notice of the claims while it was still an unnamed member of the proposed defendant class. Michigan law generally allows class-action tolling when defendants have notice of the claims and the general identities of the potential plaintiffs. But the appeals court said the existing record does not clearly establish when Allegan County received that notice.Because that question could determine whether Thompson’s claim survives, the Sixth Circuit vacated the district court’s dismissal and sent the case back for further proceedings.What happens nextThe ruling does not order Allegan County to pay Thompson the $23,500. Instead, it keeps her legal fight alive and requires the lower court to examine the notice and tolling issues again. The case also sits within a much larger Michigan dispute over foreclosure surpluses. In 2020, the Michigan Supreme Court ruled in Rafaeli, LLC v. Oakland County that counties’ retention of surplus proceeds after satisfying a property-tax debt violated the Michigan Constitution’s Takings Clause. Litigation has continued over how those principles apply to older foreclosures and how former homeowners can seek repayment.For Thompson, the immediate question is more specific: whether the earlier class action paused the legal deadline for her claim. If it did, her effort to recover the $23,500 surplus can continue.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Florida woman rode 7,000 miles through 48 states in six days, then donated $17,560 to the house that supported her when her 2-pound newborn spent nearly three months in intensive care
articles.summary: A Florida woman has completed a 7,000-mile motorcycle ride through 48 US states in six days and used the journey to raise $17,560 for Quantum House, CW34
articles.body: A Florida woman has completed a 7,000-mile motorcycle ride through 48 US states in six days and used the journey to raise $17,560 for Quantum House, CW34 reported on Monday. The organisation had supported her more than two decades ago when her newborn daughter spent nearly three months in hospital.The Palm Beach County woman, known as Jess Rips on social media, began the ride on May 12. She covered an average of more than 1,100 miles a day while travelling from Vermont to Washington. Her longest stretch on the road lasted 23 hours.Jess, who has been riding motorcycles since she was 18, also became the fastest documented woman to complete the 48-state ride. But the journey was not only about setting a record, but she wanted to use the attention surrounding the ride to raise money and awareness for Quantum House, a pediatric hospitality house that had helped her family during a difficult period.The connection goes back 22 years, when Jess's daughter was born weighing just two pounds and one ounce. The baby spent nearly three months at St Mary's Medical Center, and there were days when doctors were unsure whether she would survive. During that period, Quantum House gave Jess somewhere to stay close to her daughter.The journey: Six days and 48 statesJess said she set herself a target of completing the motorcycle journey in six days. “I started on May 12th of this year, 2026, and the goal was six days,” she said as quoted by CW34.Completing that schedule meant spending long hours on the motorcycle every day. She averaged more than 1,100 miles daily, while her longest single-day ride kept her on the road for 23 hours. “It was exhausting,” Jess said. “Between the weather changes, the traffic, it was a lot mentally and physically,” she said. Despite the difficult conditions, she completed the 7,000-mile journey within her six-day target.Jess had expected the unusual challenge to attract attention, particularly online, and decided before starting that she wanted to turn that interest towards Quantum House. “When I thought about doing this ride, and I knew it was something that was so crazy that people were going to get pumped about, especially online, I thought that this would just be a great opportunity to raise awareness for this,” she said.When Quantum House helped JessTwenty-two years earlier, Jess' daughter had been born weighing two pounds and one ounce and remained at St Mary's Medical Center for nearly three months. “There were many days where they called me, and they didn't know if she was going to make it,” Jess recalled.Quantum House provided Jess with a place to stay while her daughter was receiving treatment. That meant she could remain close to the hospital without facing the additional financial pressure of arranging accommodation.For Jess, however, the support went beyond having somewhere to sleep. She was also surrounded by other parents facing similar situations.“It was such an amazing experience because not only was I able to stay here and it relieved that financial burden on my family, but I was also provided other families and mothers that were going through the same thing and it gave me the opportunity to have somebody to talk to,” she said.The organisation continues to help families by taking care of practical needs while their children are receiving medical care.“For the families that come here, it reduces such a burden when it comes to cost,” Quantum House President and CEO Greg Quattlebaum said. “It’s a place where they can stay and they don't have to worry about where they sleep, where they wash their clothes, what am I going to eat, where do I socialize, how do I take care of all those social determinants of health, Quantum House does that,” he adds.The 'full circle moment'The motorcycle journey eventually raised $17,560 for Quantum House. When Jess returned to present the cheque, she brought both of her daughters with her. That included the daughter whose birth had first brought her to Quantum House more than two decades earlier. “So she got to see where I stayed at when I was caring for her and that was really a full circle moment,” Jess said..Her 7,000-mile journey, including the difficulties and setbacks she faced while trying to finish the ride, was also documented on her YouTube channel, Rips Unfiltered.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Ford factory in Mexico was facing pigeon invasions, forcing 4,000 workers to deal with bird poo, then a hawk named El Charro was hired and cut bird activity by 80%
articles.summary: Ford’s Hermosillo assembly plant in Sonora, Mexico, found itself dealing with an unusual workplace problem involving persistent pigeons entering the
articles.body: Ford’s Hermosillo assembly plant in Sonora, Mexico, found itself dealing with an unusual workplace problem involving persistent pigeons entering the sprawling factory and leaving droppings around equipment and freshly painted vehicles. The facility employs more than 4,000 workers and produces more than 300,000 vehicles a year, making the bird problem difficult to ignore. Ford tried conventional deterrents, including predator sounds and fake predator eyes, but the pigeons gradually became accustomed to them. The company eventually turned to a more natural solution by bringing in a trained Harris’s hawk named El Charro. Since July 2025, the hawk has patrolled the facility for several hours a day, with Ford reporting an approximately 80% decline in bird activity in monitored areas.Pigeon invasions at Ford’s Mexico factoryThe pigeon problem at Ford’s Hermosillo plant was more than an occasional nuisance. Birds repeatedly found their way into the facility, while their droppings created hygiene concerns and could end up on vehicles and around machinery. With thousands of employees working across the massive manufacturing complex, keeping the birds away became an ongoing challenge. Ford initially tried methods designed to make the factory appear unsafe for pigeons. These included sounds associated with predatory birds and visual deterrents resembling the eyes of predators. But the pigeons eventually learned that the threats were not real. Their persistence reportedly reached the point where they could wait for factory doors to open before entering.Ford turns to a real predatorAfter artificial deterrents failed to solve the problem, Ford turned to falconry. In July 2025, the company brought in El Charro, a trained Harris’s hawk, to patrol the facility. The species, Parabuteo unicinctus, is native to the Americas and is widely used in professional bird-control operations. The purpose of El Charro’s presence is primarily deterrence. His presence signals to pigeons that a genuine predator is nearby, encouraging them to leave the area or avoid settling there in the first place.El Charro patrols the plantEl Charro typically spends around two to three hours a day patrolling the Ford facility. Before his patrol, he is fed, allowing the operation to focus on controlling bird activity rather than relying on him to hunt pigeons for food. The hawk also helps identify areas where pigeons gather or build nests. Once those locations are identified, workers can remove nests and address places where birds repeatedly congregate. According to Ford, El Charro has completed more than 300 flights and logged more than 1,170 hours of patrol time since he began working at the plant.Bird activity drops by about 80%Ford says the unusual strategy has produced a substantial improvement. Bird activity in the monitored areas has fallen by about 80% since the hawk began patrolling the facility. The figure refers specifically to bird activity in monitored areas and should not be interpreted as an 80% reduction in the overall pigeon population. El Charro’s role is part of a broader bird-control programme that combines predator deterrence with nest removal and other measures. The use of trained birds of prey for bird control is already established in several industries. Airports, landfills, agricultural sites and other large facilities sometimes use falcons or hawks to discourage unwanted birds from gathering in areas where they can cause safety, hygiene or operational problems.From pest control to factory celebrityEl Charro has also become an unusual presence among workers at the Hermosillo plant. Employees have been photographed with the hawk, and Ford has highlighted him as an unconventional member of the factory workforce. His success illustrates the difference between artificial and natural deterrents. Pigeons were able to become accustomed to recorded predator sounds and fake predator images, but the presence of a trained raptor creates a genuine predator threat. For Ford, a persistent pigeon problem at one of its largest manufacturing facilities has therefore produced an unusual solution. Instead of continuing to rely only on fake predators, the company brought in a real one, turning El Charro into one of the factory’s most unconventional workers.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A Delaware homeowner who represented herself in court has secured part of the relief she sought from her community’s developer, but not everything she
articles.body: A Delaware homeowner who represented herself in court has secured part of the relief she sought from her community’s developer, but not everything she asked for. The court ordered the developer to address maintenance problems involving ponds and ditches and provide information and documents concerning an alleged $44,329.59 loan involving the homeowners association. According to an October 5, 2026 order from the Delaware Court of Chancery, the ruling came after the developer failed to defend the case, leading to a partial default judgment. The court’s order, in Colston v. The Greens at Wyoming Homeowners Association, Inc., also rejected some of the homeowner’s other requests, including certain books-and-records claims.Homeowner took the case to court herselfThe dispute involved Gwendolyn Colston, a homeowner in The Greens at Wyoming community in Delaware, and the community’s homeowners association (HOA) and developer. Colston represented herself in the litigation, meaning she proceeded without an attorney. Her lawsuit raised several issues involving the community, its homeowners association and the developer, including the condition and maintenance of ponds and drainage ditches. She also sought information concerning a $44,329.59 loan that she alleged was connected to the HOA.According to the Delaware Court of Chancery’s October 5 order, the developer failed to appear, plead or otherwise defend the case, leading Colston to seek a default judgment. A default judgment does not automatically mean every allegation made by a plaintiff is accepted or that every remedy requested must be granted. The court still has to determine what relief is legally available based on the claims and evidence before it.Court orders pond and ditch maintenanceOne of the main areas where Colston obtained relief concerned the community’s ponds and ditches. The court found that the applicable Delaware environmental provisions supported injunctive relief requiring maintenance. As a result, the developer was ordered to take steps concerning the maintenance of the community’s ponds and ditches.The order is significant because Colston had sought action over conditions affecting drainage and water-management features within the development. Rather than awarding her money for those claims, the court directed the appropriate maintenance-related relief. The distinction matters. The court specifically explained that the statutory provisions at issue allowed for injunctive relief but did not provide a private right of action for monetary damages. Therefore, Colston could obtain an order requiring action, but she could not use those provisions to secure a financial award for the alleged violations.Dispute over the $44,329.59 HOA loanAnother part of the case focused on an alleged loan of $44,329.59. Colston sought information and documents relating to the loan, including records that could help explain the transaction and its connection to the homeowners association. The court granted relief requiring the developer to confirm whether it had taken out such a loan and, if so, provide information and documents concerning it. That gives Colston a way to obtain records that she said were relevant to understanding the HOA’s financial dealings.The loan issue was separate from the court’s ruling on the broader books-and-records claim. The court did not simply order the defendants to turn over every HOA record requested by Colston.Not every claim was successfulAlthough Colston won important portions of the case, the ruling was not a complete victory. The court rejected her books-and-records claim because it was directed against the wrong party and did not meet the requirements under Delaware law. That means the default judgment did not give Colston everything she had sought in the lawsuit.The court's approach also illustrates the limits of a default judgment. Even when a defendant fails to contest a case, the plaintiff still has to establish a legal basis for the particular remedy being requested.What the ruling means for the communityFor residents of The Greens at Wyoming, the order addresses practical issues involving the development’s infrastructure as well as questions surrounding an alleged HOA loan. The pond and ditch provisions could require the developer to take action to keep those features properly maintained. Meanwhile, the disclosure concerning the $44,329.59 loan could provide additional information about the financial transaction at the centre of that part of the dispute. The case also highlights how a homeowner representing herself can pursue claims in the Delaware Court of Chancery, while showing that success on one part of a lawsuit does not necessarily extend to every claim or remedy.The October 5 order therefore leaves Colston with a mixed result: she obtained court-ordered relief concerning pond and ditch maintenance and secured disclosure tied to the alleged $44,329.59 loan, but the court declined other requests. The ruling came from the Delaware Court of Chancery, which handled the dispute and determined the scope of relief available under the claims before it.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: Saudi-backed Yemeni military forces have claimed to have “secured” the Bab al-Mandab, a strategic Red Sea waterway, in a major offensive against
articles.body: Saudi-backed Yemeni military forces have claimed to have “secured” the Bab al-Mandab, a strategic Red Sea waterway, in a major offensive against Iran-aligned Houthi rebels, the BBC reported.The military said its forces had secured key positions around the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait as part of the offensive aimed at pushing back recent Houthi advances along Yemen’s western coast.The offensive, dubbed Operation Yemen Dawn, was launched with Saudi air support as Yemeni government forces advanced along the Red Sea coast, with the military saying it had retaken key positions near the strategic waterway.Saudi-led coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Malki said 100 fighter jets were supporting the operation, while Yemeni forces said they had captured Dhubab airport, a key position south of the port city of Mokha.The Yemeni military also said its forces had recaptured the strategic port city of Mokha, a key position on the Red Sea coast. However, the claim could not be independently verified, with reports indicating that government forces had reached the city's outskirts as Houthi fighters withdrew.The Houthis denied losing control of Bab al-Mandab and Mokha, while claiming to have launched retaliatory strikes on Riyadh airport and other targets in Saudi Arabia following the Saudi-led air strikes.Saudi Arabia condemned the Houthi attacks and called on the permanent members of the UN Security Council to support Yemen's internationally recognised government. Meanwhile, Saudi allies Turkey and Pakistan held an emergency meeting in Riyadh and agreed to rapidly deploy military forces to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement.UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres also condemned what he called the Houthis' “continued cross-border attacks” on Saudi Arabia, warning that he was “deeply concerned by the sharp escalation in fighting”, AFP reported.The escalation has raised fresh concerns over the security of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, one of the world's key maritime chokepoints.The waterway connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and is a crucial route for ships travelling between the Indian Ocean and the Suez Canal, making the latest fighting a potential threat to global shipping and energy supplies.You use AI every day. articles.title: Nobel Prize in Physics awarded to Francis Halzen for groundbreaking work on cosmic neutrinos
articles.summary: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 has been awarded to Francis Halzen for “decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of
articles.body: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 has been awarded to Francis Halzen for “decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin," the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced on Tuesday.Francis Halzen is a Belgian-American physicist and professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, where he has been a leading figure in neutrino physics.Born in Tienen, Belgium, in 1944, Halzen has played a central role in the development of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory at the South Pole, a massive detector designed to study elusive neutrinos. His work helped establish the detection of high-energy neutrinos originating from astrophysical sources, opening a new way of observing and studying the universe.Halzen was instrumental in recognising that the enormous volume of transparent Antarctic ice could serve as a detector for the fleeting flashes produced when high-energy neutrinos interact with matter. He developed the concept of embedding thousands of light sensors deep in the ice to identify and reconstruct these rare interactions. This approach ultimately became IceCube, enabling researchers to trace high-energy neutrinos back to astrophysical sources and use them as messengers from distant cosmic environments. His work helped establish neutrino astronomy as a new way of studying the universe.The Nobel Prize in Physics was one of the prizes established in Alfred Nobel's will in 1895. Nobel dedicated one part of his fortune to the person who had made the “most important discovery or invention within the field of physics”.The prize is awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm. It was first awarded in 1901.Through 2025, the Physics prize had been awarded 119 times to 230 laureates, including five women. The 2026 Nobel Prize comes with 12 million Swedish kronor, to be shared if there is more than one laureate.The youngest Physics laureate is Lawrence Bragg, who was 25 when he won the prize in 1915. The oldest is Arthur Ashkin, who was 96 when he received the award in 2018. Other prominent winners include Albert Einstein who was awarded in 1921 while John Bardeen was the only person to receive it twice.Meawnhile, last year John Clarke, Michel H Devoret and John M Martinis won the Physics Nobel “for the discovery of macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit”.You use AI every day. articles.title: INDIA bloc protest: Scrap SIR, restore deleted names, sack CEC Gyanesh Kumar - key demands
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Tuesday stepped up its protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with opposition parties demanding his
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Tuesday stepped up its protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with opposition parties demanding his resignation, scrapping of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and restoration of deleted names from electoral rolls.The demands were raised as INDIA bloc MPs marched from Parliament towards the Election Commission of India headquarters in New Delhi, alleging irregularities in the electoral roll revision process.Congress's key demandsCEC's resignation: The opposition demanded the immediate removal and resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged unilateral changes to voter registration forms and centralisation of power.Scrap SIR, restore old rolls: The bloc called for suspension and repeal of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision process and sought the use of pre-SIR electoral rolls.Notice before deletion: The opposition demanded that voters receive prior notice and have access to a formal and transparent appeal mechanism before their names are removed from electoral rolls.Simpler first-time registration: The bloc called for a simpler and more accessible voter registration process for first-time and young voters.Return to ballot papers: The opposition also demanded the scrapping of Electronic Voting Machines and a return to traditional ballot paper voting.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accused the government of trying to undermine citizens' voting rights and alleged that the Election Commission was functioning at the government's direction."Look, we are fighting against the injustice of the fact that the government is stripping away everything—all the rights of the people. And today, the universal adult franchise that we received after Independence—this government is working to finish it off," Kharge said.He alleged that the CEC was "merely a puppet of the government" and claimed the poll panel acted according to directions from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah."And the Election Commission, the CEC is merely a puppet of the government. Whatever Modi and Shah tell them to do, that is exactly what they do," he said.Kharge further alleged that such functioning of institutions would harm democracy and the Constitution."Because of this, democracy will be destroyed in this country, the Constitution will be finished, and Hitler-like rule will take over," he said.Opposition targets SIR, voter formsCongress MP Karti Chidambaram alleged that the SIR exercise was disenfranchising citizens and questioned changes made to Forms 6 and 7."This is a very, very serious issue. Anybody over the age of 18 and a citizen of India has a fundamental right to vote. But the exercise of the SIR, undertaken by the Election Commission of India, is disenfranchising our citizens from their fundamental right," Chidambaram said.He said Form 6, which is used for enrolling first-time voters, contains questions about whether an applicant's parents and grandparents were voters and where they voted."Your right to vote is not dependent on the fact whether your parents were voters or not. This is not a question which can be asked in Form 6. Who inserted these questions into Form 6? If you can't go past that question, you can't enroll yourself as a voter," he said.Chidambaram also questioned whether the Election Commission had taken the decisions unanimously or through a majority."The Chief Election Commissioner cannot take decisions unilaterally. If these decisions were taken unilaterally by the Chief Election Commissioner, then it's an illegal decision, and the entire exercise is completely illegal and ultra vires," he said.On Form 7, Chidambaram alleged that the process meant for reporting voters who had died or moved away was being used for mass deletion of names."It has been brought to light in Karnataka that one party worker of the BJP has filed 7,000 Form 7 applications to delete voters," he alleged."This is a complete abuse of the process. There is an illegality, abuse of process, and disenfranchisement happening in the SIR, which is depriving the right to vote, which is fundamental to us," he said.Chidambaram demanded that the Election Commission reform itself and Kumar resign."So, the Election Commission must immediately reform itself, and the Chief Election Commissioner must resign forthwith," he said.Kharge warns of continued protestKharge accused the government of trying to take away rights secured after Independence and said protecting voting rights was essential for safeguarding democracy and the Constitution.“Rajiv Gandhi ji has given the rights to the young voters, women voters, farmers, poor people who have been given the rights after independence. Today, the Modi government is trying to snatch away those rights,” Kharge said."If we have a vote, democracy will be saved. If our democracy is saved, then everyone's rights will be protected. The Constitution will also be protected," Kharge said.He also accused the Election Commission of ignoring objections raised by its own members and alleged that electoral processes had been conducted incorrectly."When your nominated members, your people, made a mistake when they spoke, then they made a wrong election and our people today, they have tried to mislead them and come to power," he said.Kharge further warned those in power to leave office."That is why we are doing this. First, leave the seat. Otherwise, there will be a commotion in the country. The people of the country will not sit quietly. This is my warning to them," he said."People will do everything, but they are not ready to leave their freedom. The government should be destroyed," Kharge added.Congress MP Rajeev Shukla also demanded Kumar's resignation."It is certain that Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign; people have lost faith in the Election Commission," Shukla said.Congress MP Syed Nasir Hussain said, "Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar should go. SIR should be scrapped. All the deleted votes should be put back into the voters' list. A high-level inquiry should be conducted to find out the forces behind this conspiracy and to be exposed."The INDIA bloc's protest is part of its broader "Save Democracy" campaign against the Election Commission. Opposition leaders have been holding demonstrations and public programmes over electoral roll-related issues.The march towards Nirvachan Sadan has further intensified the confrontation between the opposition and the poll panel over the SIR process and electoral roll revisions.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A 1928 Los Angeles estate once owned by Casablanca director Michael Curtiz and Gene Hackman was sold for $1.71 million in 1994; 32 years later, it is back on the market asking $5.995 million
articles.summary: A nearly century-old English Cotswold-style manor in Los Angeles, once owned by Casablanca director Michael Curtiz and actor Gene Hackman, is on the
articles.body: A nearly century-old English Cotswold-style manor in Los Angeles, once owned by Casablanca director Michael Curtiz and actor Gene Hackman, is on the market. The cobblestone driveway stretching more than 200 feet leads to a manor straight out of the English countryside. Located at 4934 Queen Florence Lane in Woodland Hills, in the San Fernando Valley, the house is asking $5.995 million, Mansion Global reported.A Cotswold manor in the ValleyBuilt in 1928 by developer Harold Ferguson as his residence, the house was deeply inspired by the aesthetics of the Cotswolds, a region of England known for stone cottages and rolling hills. According to listing agent Deanna D’Egidio of Harcourts Plus, Ferguson “built this as his own residence, as an English Cotswolds manor.”The house was the centrepiece of the Canoga Estate, a far bigger property that has since been split up. It is now almost 100 years old, and the listing calls it ‘one of the most historically significant private homes’ in the San Fernando Valley.In the 1930s, Ferguson sold the estate to Michael Curtiz, who directed more than 100 films, including ‘The Adventures of Robin Hood’ and ‘White Christmas’. He won the Oscar for Best Director for ‘Casablanca’. Curtiz commissioned changes to the property, and blueprints from 1935 document the work, the listing said.The house has had some famous owners, including business magnate Walter Weisman. Gene Hackman, the Oscar-winning star of ‘The French Connection’, owned the home around 1970, according to D’Egidio.The manor now stands on over 2 acres of property and has every bit of its English countryside charm. “You have 160 rose bushes, meandering garden paths, a pond, a tennis court, a massive grass lawn. It feels like you’re in Europe, not in Los Angeles anymore,” D’Egidio said.According to D’Egidio, the property ‘has been maintained meticulously and is in original condition’ over its almost 100-year existence.From $1.71 million to $5.995 millionThe home was sold for $1.71 million in October 1994, according to public records. The house went on the market this June at $5.995 million, roughly 3.5 times that price. That is a jump of about $4.3 million since 1994. At today’s asking price, it works out to roughly $926 per square foot, according to listing data. The listing agent said the seller bought the home 35 years ago.D’Egidio worked with designer Francesca Grace and the seller’s own antique furniture to stage the rooms. “We really wanted to honour the timelessness [of the home],” she said, since buyers these days increasingly favour period charm.“What we’ve seen in L.A. is so many builders who are butchering these homes, everything looks the same. Buyers are craving authenticity, craving something timeless, craving warmth and romance.”The listing calls the home a “once-in-a-generation opportunity” to look after a piece of Los Angeles history.What the buyer getsThe manor sits on 2.09 acres of estate. The main house is 4,847 square feet. A 1,352-square-foot guest house has two dedicated changing rooms for pool days, and a separate 275-square-foot recreation room brings the total to 6,474 square feet. The main house alone is just under 5,000 square feet. There are six bedrooms and nine bathrooms, of which six are full. Hand-hewn wood floors run through the home. There are vaulted ceilings with wood beams, original leaded windows and doors, and hand-painted bathroom tiles. Leaded windows are glass panes set in thin strips of lead. Outside are copper gutters and a slate roof.The cobblestone driveway is one of the most attractive features of the manor. It has been maintained meticulously and is in original condition.Then come the grounds. A pool and a tennis court share space with a koi pond and a wide lawn that the listing says was once a croquet field. Garden paths wind past oak trees, Deodar cedars, which are large evergreens, and rose gardens.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Drones strike two vessels in Bulgaria's economic zone; one ship sinks
articles.summary: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev on Tuesday said two commercial vessels were struck by drones inside the country's Exclusive Economic Zone, marking
articles.body: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev on Tuesday said two commercial vessels were struck by drones inside the country's Exclusive Economic Zone, marking the first attack on shipping in the exclusive waters of a Nato country.The ships were attacked by several drones about 128 kilometres off Bulgaria’s coast, Radev said, after he held an emergency meeting on the incident.One of the vessels, the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan, suffered critical structural damage and sank on the spot. Officials had no immediate information about what happened to the crew, Radev said.The other ship, the Able, sailing under the Palau flag, burst into flames following the attack. A Bulgarian ferry rescued all 18 crew members. Two of them were seriously hurt and were airlifted to a hospital in the port city of Varna, the PM informed.However, the origin of the drones remains unknown.A day earlier, a Turkish-owned cargo ship carrying grain was also struck in the Black Sea and ultimately sank after catching fire, killing an Indian and an Azerbaijani citizen.Exclusive Economic ZoneUnlike a nation's territorial waters, which extend 12 nautical miles from the coast and are treated as sovereign land, an EEZ extends up to 200 nautical miles.In this zone, the coastal state only has functional economic rights like fishing, oil drilling, and mining rather than total sovereignty. Other nations still retain high seas freedoms, such as navigation and overflight.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Boost for aerial surveillance: DRDO conducts flight-trial of high-altitude platform at 21km height
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In a boost for the country's aerial surveillance capabilities, Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has carried out the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a boost for the country's aerial surveillance capabilities, Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has carried out the successful flight trial of an indigenously developed high-altitude platform (HAPS). The experimental flight attained an altitude of 21 km above mean sea level and remained at an altitude of 20 km for more than 30 minutes, before it was commanded to descend back to the ground.The system was successfully recovered, and flight performance data was analysed, a defence ministry’s release said on Tuesday. An HAPS is a lighter-than-air stratospheric system designed for long-endurance aerial surveillance, intelligence gathering and earth observation.Defence minister Rajnath Singh has complimented DRDO, IAF, PSUs and industry on the successful flight trial of HAPS and stated that the “successful trial is an important milestone in India’s Aatmanirbhar Bharat journey towards realising a long-endurance stratospheric airship”.The high-altitude platform, a lighter-than-air system as a long-endurance stratospheric aerial surveillance platform, is being designed and developed by Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE), Agra.Real-time video data and all other vehicle parameters were acquired from the airborne platform at the ground control station during the entire flight, which showed the intended flight performance. The system carried various instrumentation and control electronic packages like an inertial measurement unit, global positioning system receiver, onboard cameras, altitude control mechanism, besides various other sub-systems. The trial was conducted in coordination with various agencies, including IAF, DGCA, Airports Authority of India (AAI), Centre for Military Airworthiness and Certification and other civil authorities.Defence secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh has congratulated the teams associated with the flight trial of the high-altitude airship platform.

articles.title: 'Once a skunk, always a skunk': DMK questions Rahul Gandhi's stand on Tamil Nadu SIR deletions amid anti-CEC protest
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former Congress ally DMK on Tuesday questioned Rahul Gandhi over his stand on SIR-related deletions in Tamil Nadu, even as the Congress MP led
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Congress ally DMK on Tuesday questioned Rahul Gandhi over his stand on SIR-related deletions in Tamil Nadu, even as the Congress MP led an opposition protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi.DMK spokesperson Sarvanan Annadurai called Rahul Gandhi a "skunk" and accused him of being "duplicitous"."What’s the stand of @RahulGandhi with regard to the deletions through SIR in TN? Why is he not endorsing Kharge ji's statement that all state governments elected after SIR should be dissolved?" Sarvanan Annadurai posted on X, referring to Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge.He further asked whether Rahul Gandhi was not speaking about SIR-related deletions in Tamil Nadu out of "fear" of chief minister C Joseph Vijay, whose Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) is a Congress ally."What a duplicitous man? Once a skunk, always a skunk," the DMK spokesperson added.The DMK snapped ties with the Congress and left the Congress-led INDIA bloc after the party decided to support TVK, which emerged as the single largest party in the Tamil Nadu assembly elections in April. TVK governs the state with the support of the Congress, Left parties and the IUML.The DMK, which was voted out of power in Tamil Nadu after a single term, did not attend the INDIA bloc's September 30 meeting in Delhi, where the opposition alliance decided to march to the Election Commission (EC) office on October 6.The INDIA bloc and other groups are demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar after The Indian Express reported last month that the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had lodged at least 14 formal objections over the past 10 months, claiming that the poll body took several decisions, including those related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, without their knowledge.The EC is required to take decisions unanimously or by a 2-1 majority. However, the poll body said disagreements are "normal" in multi-member institutions and that all decisions were ultimately taken unanimously.On Monday, the Supreme Court issued notices to the EC and the Centre on a plea seeking Kumar's suspension and the cancellation of all decisions allegedly taken without the knowledge of Sandhu and Joshi. However, the top court refused to pass any interim order, saying it could not do so solely on the basis of a media report that may or may not be accurate.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
